record.original_question: Let f_lambda(z) = lambda z + z^2 with lambda = exp(2 pi i theta), and suppose theta is irrational so that f_lambda is a Cremer polynomial, meaning it is not analytically conjugate to a rotation near 0. In the Julia set of such a Cremer polynomial, is there an arc joining the fixed point 0 to its preimage -lambda?

evidence.quote: Let fλ(z) = λz + z 2 where λ = exp(2πiθ). Call such a polynomial parabolic if θ is rational. If θ is irrational, and fλ is analytically conjugate to a rotation near 0 we say fλ is a Siegel polynomial. Otherwise we call fλ a Cremer polynomial.
Question 1. Is there an arc joining 0 to −λ, in the Julia set of a Cremer polynomial? ( −λ is the preimage of the fixed point.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For $\lambda = e^{2\pi i \theta}$ with $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, consider the quadratic polynomial $f_\lambda(z) = \lambda z + z^2$, which fixes the origin with multiplier $\lambda$. Assume $\theta$ is irrational and that $f_\lambda$ is not analytically (equivalently, topologically) conjugate to the rotation $z \mapsto \lambda z$ in any neighborhood of $0$; such an $f_\lambda$ is called a Cremer polynomial, and $0$ is its Cremer fixed point. Let $J(f_\lambda) \subset \mathbb{C}$ denote the Julia set of $f_\lambda$, i.e. the closure of the set of repelling periodic points (equivalently, the complement of the Fatou set). Note that $-\lambda$ is the unique other preimage of $0$ under $f_\lambda$, and both $0$ and $-\lambda$ belong to $J(f_\lambda)$.

Question: For every Cremer polynomial $f_\lambda$, does the Julia set $J(f_\lambda)$ contain an arc (a homeomorphic image of the closed interval $[0,1]$) whose endpoints are $0$ and $-\lambda$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question about the existence of an arc joining the Cremer fixed point 0 to its preimage -λ in the Julia set of a quadratic Cremer polynomial appears to remain open. Subsequent work by Blokh, Childers, Oversteegen, Sørensen and others has established striking topological properties of Cremer Julia sets (non-local connectivity, examples with positive area, degenerate impressions, external rays accumulating on both 0 and -λ), but no result fully resolving the existence (or nonexistence) of such an arc for all Cremer polynomials was found.

status_evidence.title: The Julia sets of quadratic Cremer polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Sørensen constructed basic Cremer polynomials with external rays which accumulate on both the Cremer point and its preimage.
status_evidence.claim: Related structural results about Cremer Julia sets are known, but the arc question is discussed as an open problem about topology of these Julia sets.

status_evidence.title: Monotone images of Cremer Julia sets (Blokh–Oversteegen)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the topology of Julia sets of quadratic Cremer polynomials and their monotone images.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to probe topology of Cremer Julia sets without settling the existence of an arc from 0 to -λ.

status_evidence.title: On (non)local connectivity of quadratic Julia sets (arXiv:0812.1239)
status_evidence.snippet: There exist quadratic Cremer Julia sets of positive area with degenerate impressions for a full-measure set of angles.
status_evidence.claim: Partial topological information is available but does not resolve the arc question.
